Hi Marissa —

Thanks for running the demo last week. Procurement is ready to move forward but legal has a couple of non-trivial asks before we can sign the MSA + Order Form for the private deployment (VPC/on-prem). High-level asks below — I've attached our procurement intake form. Can you confirm which of these Redwood can accommodate and provide an evidence package we can forward to our security team?

1) License scope: We need clarity that the license is non-exclusive for our deployment but includes rights to run derivative models we train on top of the supplied weights. Please include any carveouts (if derivatives are restricted).
2) Operator access & audit window: We require a 30-day audit window and a witnessed snapshot transfer procedure for forensic verification. Is there a documented runbook?
3) Data custody & encryption: KMS/HSM attestations and key custody flow — can you provide technical and contractual language?
4) Order Form exhibits: Which exhibits will we get at signing (runbook, operator SOP, SLA exhibits)?

Timeline: procurement would like redlines and evidence by EOD Friday (2026-08-20) to keep quarter close.

Attaching: Sonata_Procurement_Form.pdf

Thanks — happy to do a short call if easier. Looping our counsel Olivia (cc'ed) for visibility.

Dana Lee
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Sonata Health

Marissa / Dana —

Thanks for the detail. I've reviewed Sonata's procurement asks and sketched a redline summary so legal and procurement can converge quickly. Attached: MSA_redlines_v1.docx (high level bullets below).

Summary of proposed positions (we can negotiate these, but want to be explicit):

- License scope: propose "non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and create derivative works from the hosted model and any model outputs created using Customer-supplied data". We will add a security carveout: Redwood retains rights to internal model improvements and to use telemetry for product ops, but will not use Customer PII for model training without explicit consent.
- Derivatives: Customer may create derivative models; Redwood requests a limited license to run hosted inference on variants for compatibility testing (non-production). If Sonata needs exclusive ownership of derivatives, that would require a separate IP transfer exhibit and pricing adjustment.
- Operator access: limit to emergency/maintenance with prior notice except for audit windows agreed in writing; propose an operator-access log exhibit and an audit witness protocol.
- Audit and snapshot transfer: propose a staged evidence handover (encrypted snapshot + hash verification + signed witness attestation). Recommend we describe this in an Order Form Exhibit (Evidence & Snapshot Procedure).
- KMS/key custody: contractually, Redwood will describe integration options (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM) and provide a key-handback attestation for the deployment.

I'll attach the redline doc. If Sonata's counsel suggests alternate wording, we can track changes in the docx and converge.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: MSA_redlines_v1.docx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@sonatahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines + private deployment evidence ask

Dana / Marissa —

I'm attaching a short technical pack (privdeploy-runbook.pdf) and a snapshot-checklist.xlsx that map to the evidence items Karthik referenced. Highlights:

- Snapshot witness flow (virtual): we create a forensic snapshot, compute SHA-256 digests, and stream the encrypted blob to an S3 bucket you control. An independent witness (customer or third-party) joins the session; we record the signing of digests and produce a signed attestation.
- On-site witness: if Sonata prefers on-site, we can coordinate a time and provide a cleanroom operator to perform the export. On-site adds 3–5 business days to the timeline and requires scoped access requests in advance.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or an HSM model with an attestation letter. We'll include the key-rotation schedule and evidence of encryption-in-transit/at-rest in the pack.
- Exhibits we can deliver at signing: Runbook (privdeploy-runbook.pdf), Snapshot Checklist (snapshot-checklist.xlsx), Operator Access Log template, and an Evidence Handover Exhibit.

Requested clarifications for logistics:
- Which region will you deploy in? (affects data residency language we propose)
- Do you need a longer retention of operator logs (>90 days)?

I expect to have the pack and checklist in your inbox by EOD 2026-08-18.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Attachments: privdeploy-runbook.pdf, snapshot-checklist.xlsx

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The proposed approach looks reasonable. A few clarifications before we circulate to our InfoSec:

- Region: us-east-1 (required for our internal policy).
- Witness: virtual witness is sufficient for now; we may request on-site for future audits.
- Operator logs: 180 days retention is preferred; can Redwood confirm feasibility?
- Derivatives/IP: Sonata wants to retain full ownership of any derivative models trained solely on our data. The proposed carveout language is acceptable subject to explicit wording that prohibits Redwood from using those derivatives for its own model training or product telemetry.

Next steps: please send the redlined MSA (track changes) and the DocuSign envelope for the Order Form exhibits once the 180-day operator log retention is confirmed. Looping in Olivia to coordinate any final legal tweaks.

Appreciate the help — procurement target remains 2026-08-27 for final sign.

Dana Lee
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Sonata Health
